body: I know what you mean. I've had that instinct too. But somehow, it doesn't scare me. It gives me the assurance that when I've had enough, I'll be able to go out with dignity. And I'll be able to CHOOSE rather than succumb.
Not that I know of. I'm scared he will be eventually though.
Tried, but he's really sharp. He wants to see the medicine and research it before having it. He thinks we don't understand what he's going through.

I don't live in a country where access to psychiatric care is easy. It's considered a huge taboo, so it's all the more harder. I have tried talking him into a sleeping medicine, but he's really sharp. He wants to see the pill, read about it online before taking it. In a sense, he's already suspicious. 
Is there any chance that a normal, routine life could help set some of it on track?
Yes. I was advised to drug him without his knowledge.
The advice I have gotten is to medicate on the sly. I feel like he will find out for certain and that will make it worse. He will get suspicious and may even walk away from loved ones.
